# vendor/

Upstream source, copied in rather than fetched. **Do not edit to fix a bug or tidy a warning** —
everything here is answerable to the upstream revision below, and every deviation from it is listed
in this file. Changing anything without adding a line here makes the copy unreadable.

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | `github.com/LaihoE/demoparser` |
| Revision | `ba39cc44cd5abfd7f34df2b3c0a7dd3630048311` (2026-07-07) |
| Crates | `src/parser` → `vendor/parser`, `src/csgoproto` → `vendor/csgoproto` |
| Crate version | `parser` 0.1.1, `csgoproto` 0.1.5 — neither is published to crates.io |

`demoparser2` is the name of the PyPI and npm bindings. The Rust crate is called `parser`, which is
why the dependency in `crates/demo-parser/Cargo.toml` reads `parser` and not `demoparser2`.

## Why a copy and not a git dependency

Two things have to change in upstream before it can be used here, and neither can be expressed as a
cargo setting:

1. **`Instant::now()` traps on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`**, and `Parser::parse_demo` calls it on its
   second line. `docs/PARSER.md` §8 has the measurement; the short version is that the optimiser
   then removes the whole parser as unreachable and the artifact measures 293 KB instead of 2 MB.
2. **Both build scripts reach the network.** `csgoproto/build.rs` clones `GameTracking-CS2` and
   runs `prost-build`, which needs `protoc` on the host; `parser/build.rs` then runs `csgoproto`'s
   own binary through a nested `cargo run`.

A copy also makes the build hermetic in a way a git dependency is not: `cargo build --offline`
completes from a fresh clone with no network access at any stage.

## What was changed

### Removed, because they regenerate files that upstream already committed

`csgoproto/build.rs`, `csgoproto/src/main.rs`, `csgoproto/src/parser.rs`, `csgoproto/update_protos.py`
and `parser/build.rs`.

The three files they produce — `csgoproto/src/protobuf.rs` (`// @generated by prost-build`),
`csgoproto/src/maps.rs` and `csgoproto/src/message_type.rs` (`// Autogenerated by main.rs`) — are in
upstream's tree at the pinned revision and are kept here byte for byte. Only the `GameTracking-CS2`
checkout was gitignored upstream, never its output. Nothing here needs generating; regenerating it
is what required the network.

`csgoproto/Cargo.toml` loses its `[build-dependencies]` on `prost-build` with the script that used
it, which keeps 19 packages out of the dependency graph.

### Removed, because they do not belong in this repository

- `parser/test_demo.dem` — 60 MB. `AGENTS.md` §18 forbids committing a `.dem`, and §15 rules out
  Git LFS.
- `parser/src/e2e_test.rs` — 636 kB of tests that need that demo. Its `#[cfg(test)] pub mod
  e2e_test;` line is gone from `parser/src/lib.rs` with it.
- `parser/src/bin/parse_bench.rs` — a benchmark binary that reads a demo from disk.
- Both `Cargo.lock` files, both `.gitignore` files, both `README.md` files and both `rustfmt.toml`
  files. Resolution is our root `Cargo.lock`'s job and formatting is not applied here at all.

### Changed

- **`parser/src/parse_demo.rs`** — the two unconditional `Instant::now()` calls made lazy, in
  upstream's own `prof_on().then(std::time::Instant::now)` style. This is
  `tools/probes/wasm-build/lazy-instant.patch` applied as ordinary source rather than carried as a
  patch file. `docs/PARSER.md` §11 keeps offering this upstream as an open question.
- **`parser/Cargo.toml`** — `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.release]` removed. Cargo ignores profiles
  on a non-root package and warns about them on every build; the real profiles are in the root
  manifest.
- **`vendor/Cargo.toml`** — added. It makes `vendor/` a workspace root of its own, which is what
  keeps `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy --workspace` from answering for upstream code. It is
  paired with `exclude = ["vendor"]` in the root manifest, without which cargo refuses the nested
  root outright.
- **`[lints.rust] warnings = "allow"`** in both manifests. Upstream builds with ten warnings that
  are not ours to fix, and letting them print on every build is how a real warning from
  `crates/` goes unread.

## What was not changed, and must not be

Upstream panics on a file shorter than 16 bytes: `first_pass/parser.rs` slices
`demo_bytes[..HEADER_ENDS_AT_BYTE]` one line before its own `bytes.len() < 16` check can fire. That
is guarded in `crates/demo-parser` instead, because never crashing on a malformed file is this
repository's contract and not upstream's. Patching it here would hide the guard from the tests that
own it.

## Updating the revision

Re-copy from a fresh upstream checkout, re-apply every entry under *What was changed*, and update
the revision in the table. Then re-record the binary size in `AGENTS.md` §16 from a build that has
been **run**, never from one that merely compiled.
